title: Evaluation of ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing AI Chat Performances on Physics Exams of Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination
extended_summary:
This paper examines how well two large language model chatbots, ChatGPT and Microsoft BingChat, perform on Vietnamese high school physics exam questions. The central question is whether these systems can answer national high school graduation examination items accurately enough to be comparable to human students, and what their strengths and weaknesses reveal about their potential role in education. The study is motivated by growing interest in using AI for feedback, personalization, and support in teaching and learning, particularly in Vietnamese-language educational contexts.

The authors evaluated ChatGPT (Feb 13 version) and BingChat (April 15 version) on a subset of the VNHSGE dataset consisting of five illustrative Vietnamese national high school graduation physics exams from 2019 to 2023, totaling 200 multiple-choice questions. Questions were categorized by difficulty level: knowledge, comprehension, application, and high application. The study compares chatbot accuracy across question order and year, and also compares converted chatbot scores with Vietnamese student score distributions and averages from the national exam.

The population and context are Vietnamese high school students indirectly represented through national exam materials and national score distributions rather than direct human participation in an intervention. The setting is best characterized as lab-style evaluation of AI systems on exam questions, not a classroom implementation. The paper also discusses possible educational uses of LLMs, such as immediate feedback, individualized instruction, and generation of practice materials, but these uses were not directly tested in the study.

The main conclusion is that both ChatGPT and BingChat underperform Vietnamese students on high school physics exams and struggle especially with high application questions requiring complex reasoning. BingChat achieved somewhat higher average accuracy than ChatGPT, while ChatGPT was described as more stable or consistent across administrations. The authors conclude that LLMs are not ready to replace human expertise in physics teaching, though they may still have supportive value for students and teachers in providing feedback, individualized learning experiences, and practice content.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark-style evaluation of LLM performance on K-12 physics exam items with descriptive comparison to student score distributions, but it is not an intervention study of student learning and does not use an experimental or quasi-experimental design. It provides direct K-12 task evidence but only limited causal credibility.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported academic finding is that both LLMs underperformed Vietnamese high school students and struggled on high-application physics questions. Because no positive learning impact on students was measured and the main comparative result is unfavorable, impact is best classified as red.

interventions.use_case: Evaluating ChatGPT and Microsoft BingChat as conversational large language models answering Vietnamese national high school physics exam questions, with discussion of their possible use for individualized feedback and learning support.

finding.finding_summary: The study evaluated ChatGPT (Feb 13 version) and BingChat (April 15 version) on 200 multiple-choice high school physics questions drawn from five Vietnamese illustrative national graduation exams (2019–2023). Average accuracy was 61% for ChatGPT and 66% for BingChat, compared with Vietnamese student average converted scores of 6.39 and modal scores typically above the LLMs; both systems performed especially poorly on high-application questions, leading the authors to conclude that the LLMs underperformed human students in specialized physics reasoning. No standardized effect sizes or confidence intervals were reported.
finding.measure: Accuracy and converted exam scores on Vietnamese high school physics multiple-choice exams, including performance by question difficulty level
finding.study_size: n=200 questions across 5 illustrative exams; student comparison distributions reported for national cohorts, exact pooled comparison n not reported in analytic model
